pending_findings.summary: QueueService.reorder()'s two-phase service_order renumbering (temp value = length+index+1, then final = index+1) assumes the checked-in set's service_order values are contiguous 1..length. They are not guaranteed to be: no_show/cancel can remove any checked-in entry (only call requires 'next in order'), leaving a gap that check_in's MAX(service_order)+1 does not backfill. When a gap exists, a row's original value can land inside the temp range and collide with a not-yet-processed row mid-loop, raising a raw unhandled 23505 unique-violation on queue_entries_session_service_order_uq instead of succeeding or failing with a clean domain error.
pending_findings.evidence: https://github.com/NTinkicht/Tabibi/pull/39#issuecomment-5561043107 -- includes an independently written and run reproduction against real Postgres in a worktree (check in 3, no_show the middle one, check in a 4th, reorder the first entry to the back) that reproduces the exact duplicate-key error at src/modules/queue/index.ts:838.
pending_findings.required_resolution: Make the renumbering immune to gaps -- simplest: set service_order=NULL for every row in `reordered` first (removes them from the partial index's WHERE predicate entirely), then assign final 1..length values in a second phase. Also wrap the update(s) in a try/catch translating 23505 to QueueConflictError, matching command()'s existing pattern, as defense in depth.
pending_findings.verification_method: A regression test that no_shows or cancels a non-first checked-in entry (creating a gap), checks in another entry, then reorders -- must succeed or fail with a clean domain error, never a raw Postgres exception.
